signal.reasoning: I can understand the economics shown here: margins are high and improving, free cash flow per share exceeds earnings per share, and book value per share has risen while leverage has eased. Those are attractive signs, though four quarters do not prove a ten-year moat, and a current ratio near 1 leaves little cushion. At 37.5 times earnings, I would want more certainty about durable growth before committing to hold it for a decade; favorable product reviews and forecasts are no substitute for that margin of safety.
